meaning: A palm reading: Jupiter-type lines cutting across the marriage line on the Mercury mount, and straight lines on that mount, are read as harming children.
inference: Tradition says this palm sign damages children; a Jupiter mark on Mercury mount also shows a worldly, astrologer-like person.

meaning: A palm reading where bad Mars marks, such as an '18' marker, are tied to the fate of children and to the 3-8-13-18 house corners.
inference: Tradition links this Mars mark to loss of a child around age 8 or 18.

meaning: A palm reading of the fish line (machh rekha) pointing up with its tail at the wrist and the life line entering its mouth.
inference: Tradition reads it as a big, hospitable family with early marriage and children, and no more siblings after the year the fish body ends.

meaning: A palm reading of a Ketu mark on the Moon mount, treated like a lunar eclipse effect around ages 24 to 34.
inference: Tradition says a wise person with more daughters and a six-year loss, repaired by a good head line.

meaning: A palm reading of a Ketu mark on the bad-Mars mount of the hand.
inference: Tradition calls this very bad, with no children and trouble on all sides.

meaning: A palm reading of a Ketu mark on the Saturn mount, with age 48 as a turning point and results depending on Saturn being reversed or helped.
inference: Tradition gives mixed results: ruin of body and property if Saturn is reversed, wealth from the earth if helped.

meaning: A worked example of one hand with four sons and two daughters, linking the ages of births and marriages to Mercury, Sun and Venus periods.
inference: It only illustrates how the author reads the timing of children and wives; it is not a testable rule.

meaning: Jupiter placed in the 5th house together with, or hurt by, a malefic, or retrograde or combust.
inference: Tradition says this brings grief through children.
variants: Jupiter in 5th conjunct Rahu or Ketu

meaning: Jupiter in the 10th house either joined by a malefic or aspected by one.
inference: Tradition says this gives wrong deeds, laziness and little happiness from sons.

meaning: Mars in the 2nd, Saturn in the 3rd, and the 5th house, its lord, the 9th lord and Jupiter all afflicted.
inference: Tradition says loss of a son or childlessness.
variants: Mars in 2nd and Saturn in 3rd counted from Moon lagna

meaning: Moon, Rahu, Mercury and Jupiter all in the lagna, with Ketu alone in the 7th house.
inference: Tradition says only one son survives past 35, though the four planets still give a raja yoga.
variants: same four planets in lagna with Ketu in 7th counted from Moon

meaning: Remedies for Jupiter in the 5th house: keep a dog, do daily Ganesh puja, avoid religious begging and stay honest.
inference: Tradition says these habits ease the harm of Jupiter in the 5th to children.

meaning: The Lal Kitab author's view of the Sun placed in the 3rd house.
inference: Tradition says children are long lived, the native never really poor, and service to elders adds to life.
variants: Sun in 3rd in own or exalted sign

meaning: Remedies for the Moon in the 3rd house: donate Moon items at a daughter's birth and Sun items at a son's birth, wheat or jaggery at marriage, keep a horse or chakor.
inference: Tradition says these gifts steady family and money matters for this placement.

meaning: Mars and Ketu joining or aspecting the 5th house, its lord and Jupiter at once.
inference: Tradition says death of sons or no sons; a strong but afflicted 5th lord may lose a son.
variants: Mars-Ketu on the 5th from Moon lagna

meaning: Remedies for Mars in the 6th house: no gold on children, Saturn remedy, feed milk to six girls and give silver or rice.
inference: Tradition says these protect children born on risky weekdays under this Mars.

meaning: Mercury as lord of the 12th, joined with Jupiter or the 5th lord and aspected by Mars.
inference: Tradition says it shortens a son's life; a topaz for Jupiter is said to help.
variants: Mercury 12th lord with Jupiter for Cancer or Libra lagna

meaning: Saturn in the 2nd house with a daughter born before age 34 and married away.
inference: Tradition says she brings luck to her in-laws while the native lives on his own earnings.

meaning: Saturn in the 5th house of the annual (varshphal) chart.
inference: Tradition says no harm and no remedy is needed; children are many and long lived but not helpful to parents.
variants: annual chart Saturn in 9th for comparison

meaning: Saturn in the 2nd and Mercury in the 12th, with a daughter born.
inference: Tradition says supporting her from the native's wealth is bad, and in-laws should keep her as she is a Lakshmi to them.

meaning: Saturn in the 5th kills children, Saturn in the 9th blocks birth, and Rahu in the 5th or 9th harms the child before or after birth.
inference: Tradition says these placements threaten children; marrying the same wife twice and burying silver are the remedy.

meaning: Mars and Ketu in the 5th, Moon in a Sagittarius lagna, and Sun and Venus together in the 9th.
inference: Tradition says it destroys children and brings injury to father, thigh and body, to be eased by strengthening Mars, Sun, Venus and Jupiter.

meaning: For a bad Moon in the 11th house, the native's mother should leave when the wife's labour begins and not see the baby for 43 days.
inference: Tradition says this keeps the child safe from the bad Moon's effect on the mother.

meaning: The Sun joined with a friendly planet, versus with an enemy planet.
inference: Tradition says luck beats the father's with a friend, and children do poorly with an enemy.

meaning: Ketu and Venus placed together in any house.
inference: Tradition says they block children, and an unmarried native may go blind.

meaning: Sun and Jupiter together, acting like a good Mars.
inference: Tradition says this is very good for children.

meaning: Mars in the 6th with Ketu's effect versus Mars in the 12th with Rahu quiet, plus Mercury in 12 and no son before 34.
inference: Tradition says Mars in 6 reduces sons and Mars in 12 is milder; Mercury in 12 gives mental strain.

meaning: A bad Mars in the 12th with Mercury in the 8th and no link to Moon or Sun, softened if Sun is in the 4th.
inference: Tradition says risk to a child early in life and trouble from Rahu to children, brothers and eyes until 28.
variants: Mars in 12th with Sun in 4th as exception

meaning: Saturn in the 5th together with a bad Mars.
inference: Tradition says this harms the Moon, meaning mother and mind.

meaning: An empty 10th house with Saturn in the 5th.
inference: Tradition says it surely destroys children, unless Ketu sits in the 10th to help them survive.
variants: Saturn in 5th with Ketu in 10th as exception

meaning: Using a cot given by the in-laws at night is said to help having children and keep Ketu from turning bad.
inference: Tradition says the household cot acts as a symbol of Ketu and protects it.

meaning: For a weak Jupiter, read Shrimad Bhagavat and Harivansh Purana and do Hari puja.
inference: Tradition says this heals kin separation, marriage delay and child obstruction caused by weak Jupiter.

meaning: A remark that after a son is born progress comes, especially if a planet is in the 9th, and buying gold brings more sons.
inference: It is a folk saying about omens with no chart test.

meaning: Venus placed in an earlier house than Mercury makes Rahu bad, and Mercury earlier than Venus makes Ketu good.
inference: Tradition says the first order troubles childbirth and the second order lets the child come.
variants: Mercury in the earlier house than Venus

meaning: Venus in an earlier house with Mercury in the next house together with Venus's enemy the Sun.
inference: Tradition says the Venus-Mercury link breaks and childbirth becomes hard.
variants: Mercury in next house with Saturn instead of Sun

meaning: A weak Jupiter in the Lal Kitab sense.
inference: Tradition says loss of the father's happiness, early loss of the father, chest health strain in Jupiter periods and blocked foreign travel.

meaning: Sun and Moon in the 10th and 11th houses are called a pitar rin (ancestral debt), with causes like harming animals or snakes.
inference: Tradition says it is cured by feeding a hundred workers in a day with equal family shares.

meaning: Moon in the 2nd house of the natal chart, with Ketu in the 12th as a threat.
inference: Tradition says good education, sons, inheritance and Moon-type business success; Ketu in 12 harms education and sons.

meaning: During exams a student should not follow a fixed study timetable.
inference: Tradition says rigid schedules disturb results in this system.

meaning: During exams a student should not announce that preparation is good or that the paper went well.
inference: Tradition says boasting about results spoils them.

meaning: During exams a student should not pray to God for marks.
inference: Tradition says asking for marks is discouraged in this exam practice.

meaning: During exams a student should not take pressure about marks or compare with others.
inference: Tradition says comparison and mark anxiety hurt performance.

meaning: During exams a student should not keep testing themselves again and again by revising.
inference: Tradition says repeated self-testing is a bad habit in exam time.

meaning: After an exam a student should not discuss the paper or work out marks.
inference: Tradition says post-exam discussion harms the final result.

meaning: Students in exam time should avoid red, white, black and yellow stationery.
inference: Tradition says these colours are unhelpful for exam stationery.

meaning: Overconfidence guarantees failure, so a student should study the whole syllabus and not pick topics.
inference: Tradition says humility and full coverage protect exam results.

meaning: A pen sign on the palm, with Mercury in the 7th (placement unclear because of scan doubt).
inference: Tradition says a good writer and author of books.

meaning: Jupiter in the 1st house with the 7th occupied and no enemy planet in the 1st.
inference: Tradition says good education and a high degree, while Saturn decides financial status.
variants: Jupiter in 1st with 7th occupied from Moon lagna

meaning: Sun in the 10th house with the 4th house empty.
inference: Tradition says education and intelligence go unused; throwing a copper piece in running water for 40 or 43 days is the fix.
variants: Sun in 10th with 4th empty from Moon lagna

meaning: Venus in the 1st with Mercury in the 3rd or 6th.
inference: Tradition says excellent intellect and favourable court decisions.

meaning: Palm reading of the Sun line, with meaning by where it sits between the fingers: schooling, technical skill, handicraft, astrology, maths or yoga.
inference: Tradition says a long clean Sun line gives full learning, and its position shows the kind of skill.

meaning: Garbled text mixing Mercury in houses 3 or 6, a daughter as first child, and Gemini or Virgo giving 80 years.
inference: Cannot tell the real condition; Mercury is read as tongue, intellect, trade and clerkship.

meaning: A weak Jupiter with Mercury in the 2nd, both hurt by Saturn or Rahu.
inference: Tradition says little education, poor speech, thin finances and illness among mother's elder brothers.
variants: Jupiter weak with Mercury in 2nd and Saturn aspect
Jupiter weak with Mercury in 2nd and Rahu conjunction

meaning: Saturn and Rahu hostile to the lord of the 2nd house.
inference: Tradition says obstruction in education; coral for Mars and calming Saturn and Rahu are advised.

meaning: Saturn as 2nd lord sitting in the 6th and hurt by Rahu, especially with Mercury too.
inference: Tradition says education and speech are lost; sapphire with iron and calming Rahu help.
variants: Saturn 2nd lord in 6th conjunct Rahu and Mercury

meaning: Moon joined with Mercury while the Moon is within 72 degrees of the Sun, under Saturn influence.
inference: Tradition says loss of intellect and mental shock; a bright Moon instead gives Moon-type wealth through Mercury.
variants: Moon more than 72 degrees from the Sun as the bright case

meaning: How to read education: check the 5th lord Sun, then Jupiter in its pakka house, then the Moon, with the 4th house damaged by a benefic showing incomplete study.
inference: It gives the order of planets to inspect for education, not a single testable condition.

meaning: Palm reading of a square at the base between Venus and bad Mars, and a two-branch bad-Mars mark.
inference: Tradition says a mystery around birth and poor parents, improving when the branches join.

meaning: Palm reading of straight lines at the edge of the Moon mount running outside the palm.
inference: Tradition says they show mother's relatives; a two-branch line shows mother's sisters who spoil business.

meaning: Palm reading of a head line reaching far to the bad-Mars mount.
inference: Tradition says the native is quick-witted but his maternal uncle's family is ruined.

meaning: Palm reading of a forked head line toward bad Mars, with branches at ages 7, 14, 21 and 28.
inference: Tradition says the maternal uncle's line ends, or he leaves home at those ages.

meaning: Palm reading of straight lines on the bad-Mars edge going outside the palm; two-branch means a widowed aunt.
inference: Tradition says they show paternal uncles and aunts, and a widow aunt whose blessing should be kept.

meaning: Palm reading where a sound head line stops bad Mars from acting, and Sun in house 8 makes bad Mars act as good Mars.
inference: Tradition says a good head line cancels the Mars harm, and the missing Mars mounts mean one man faces lakhs.

meaning: Sun in house 8 is treated as having the effect of Mars-nek over the Sun's house.
inference: Tradition says such a Sun is never present at the place of death.

meaning: Palm reading of a head line with island or chain, or leaving the life line toward Jupiter, to read the parents' lives.
inference: Tradition says mother dies first if the island is above, and a clear deep line gives mother about 80 years.

meaning: Palm reading of a Ketu mark on the Sun mount.
inference: Tradition says it dims the Sun: maternal side suffers, wife's happiness is light and royal favour is small.

meaning: Palm reading of a Ketu mark on the Mars-nek mount.
inference: Tradition says it is good for self but hostile to brothers, with life abroad.

meaning: A brother indicated by Mars in house 3 together with Ketu.
inference: Tradition says the brother prospers after 42 but gives no help, and the native stands alone.

meaning: Jupiter as lord of the 7th, debilitated or weak, or joined with Mars.
inference: Tradition says the father lacks elder brothers or the brother lives unhappily; wearing pukhraj is said to help.
variants: Jupiter 7th lord with Mars for Gemini or Virgo lagna

meaning: Jupiter as lord of the 11th, weak and afflicted, mainly for an Aquarius lagna.
inference: Tradition says low own income and opposition from an elder brother.

meaning: Venus and the Moon in opposition to each other.
inference: Tradition says the mother has eye trouble.

meaning: Mercury as lord of the 11th or 4th house badly afflicted.
inference: Tradition says early death of the father.

meaning: Mercury as lord of the 8th from the 6th (the lagna), afflicted by Mars and Ketu.
inference: Tradition says loss of the mother's younger brother; emerald and shanti are advised.
variants: Gemini lagna with Mars-Ketu on Mercury
Virgo lagna with Mars-Ketu on Mercury

meaning: Gemini falling in the 3rd house (Aries lagna) with Mars influence.
inference: Tradition says arm trouble, possible loss of a hand and danger to a younger sister.

meaning: Gemini falling in the 4th house (Pisces lagna) with a malefic influence.
inference: Tradition says risk of the father's untimely death.
variants: Pisces lagna with Saturn in Gemini

meaning: Mercury afflicted while in or ruling the 9th house.
inference: Tradition says strained kin relations and special suffering for the father.

meaning: Mercury afflicted in the 9th with Mars also afflicted.
inference: Tradition says special suffering for the wife's younger brother or a younger sister's husband.

meaning: Mercury afflicted in the 10th house.
inference: Tradition says danger to the life of younger siblings; strengthen Mercury with emerald.

meaning: Mercury as lord of the 11th afflicted by Mars.
inference: Tradition says untimely death of the mother even if the Moon is strong.

meaning: Mercury and Venus together ruling the 11th, with Mars and Ketu influence.
inference: Tradition says a short life for the son's wife.

meaning: Mercury and Jupiter together with Mars and Ketu influence.
inference: Tradition says a short life for the son-in-law; topaz is advised.

meaning: Mercury and Mars together with Ketu and Saturn influence.
inference: Tradition says short life for the father's younger brothers or sisters; coral is advised.

meaning: Mercury and Jupiter together, afflicted by Mars and Ketu.
inference: Tradition says short life of the elder brother; strengthen Jupiter with topaz.

meaning: Rahu and Ketu are said to spoil Saturn, and Venus becomes the scapegoat for Saturn's clashes.
inference: Tradition says the wife can fall ill, so Venus must be kept in good condition.

meaning: A bad Rahu affects the wife's brother and sister's husband, calmed by a Moon remedy or a strong Mars.
inference: Tradition says in-law relatives suffer under a bad Rahu.

meaning: Ketu with the Moon (like an eclipse), and Venus with the Moon making Ketu debilitated.
inference: Tradition says a debilitated Ketu brings wasting illness to son and grandson, but is good if Jupiter and Mars are absent.

meaning: Moon within 72 degrees of the Sun with Mars, harming both lordships, with a worked Aquarius lagna case.
inference: Tradition says loss of a younger brother and mother's suffering when Moon-Mars aspect the 4th.

meaning: For a bad Mars in the 7th, serve the brother's children.
inference: Tradition says serving 9th-house relatives eases the Mars harm.

meaning: Three planets joined together while the Moon is with a malefic at birth.
inference: Tradition says possible death of the mother.

meaning: Three planets joined together while the Sun is with malefics.
inference: Tradition says possible death of the father.

meaning: Sun and Mars together with Moon and Ketu.
inference: Tradition says illness of a son, maternal uncle or father.

meaning: The Sun's own period is good for itself but makes Venus's whole period bad, and the Moon gives the Sun 25 percent help.
inference: Tradition says one planet's good time can cost another planet's results.

meaning: Venus loves Saturn and sacrifices itself when any planet strikes Saturn.
inference: Tradition says Venus matters (wife, comforts) take the damage meant for Saturn.

meaning: Venus and the Moon in opposition, said to harm the mother's eyesight.
inference: Same claim as the earlier Venus-Moon opposition rule: trouble for the mother's eyes.

meaning: Sun and Mars together with Venus and Ketu.
inference: Tradition says illness of the wife, son or mother, and of the father if Moon and Jupiter join in.

meaning: The Moon on one side and the Sun on the other side of Mars, in neighbouring houses.
inference: Tradition says parents die or leave around ages 13 to 18, and a sister is either happy like a queen or unmarried.
variants: Sun in house before Mars and Moon in house after
Moon before Mars and Sun after

meaning: Mars in the 3rd with Jupiter or Sun in the 9th or 11th, or Moon or Mercury in the 9th or 11th.
inference: Tradition says self-made bad luck, but family and rich in-laws help.

meaning: Mars and Mercury in the 3rd with Jupiter, Sun or Moon in the 7th.
inference: Tradition says the native's own state is poor but in-laws fully help.

meaning: A bad Mars in the 4th or 7th, with different results in Saturn's houses.
inference: Tradition says it destroys spouse and wealth, hurts a brother in one Saturn house and a son in both, and makes tasks crooked.

meaning: A bad Mars reaches the houses of male planets (Sun in 5, Jupiter in 2, 5, 9, 11) or of female planets (Venus, Moon) in the Lal Kitab house-ownership sense.
inference: Tradition says wealth and men are hurt through male planets' houses, and women suffer through the female ones.

meaning: A Lal Kitab afflicted Mars sitting in the 2nd house is said to make the native quarrelsome and hard on brothers, with the harm coming mostly from inside the household.
inference: Family peace, brothers and the father's luck suffer, mostly from within the home; the harm lessens if Ketu is also in the 2nd.
variants: Ketu also in 2nd house (native rules well)

meaning: A Lal Kitab afflicted Mars in the 3rd house is said to bring enmity with uncles, aunts and brothers and repeated illness.
inference: Strained ties with paternal and maternal relatives and poor health; Mercury joining Mars removes the bad result.
variants: Mercury with Mars in 3rd house cancels the harm

meaning: A Lal Kitab afflicted Mars in the 8th house gives a person skilled in fight schemes, with trouble for the wife and fear around life after marriage.
inference: Marriage-linked suffering and fear; the 8th is not treated as a death house if Sun or Jupiter is in the 4th.
variants: Sun in 4th house softens the result
Jupiter in 4th house softens the result

meaning: When Mercury, whose own Virgo house is the 3rd in the Lal Kitab layout, moves into the 5th house, the book says the native has no brother and one arm is weak.
inference: Loss of sibling support and some weakness in an arm.

meaning: Mercury in the 2nd house with Jupiter in the 6th or 7th is said to give little happiness from the father, with his protective cover ending around age 19.
inference: Reduced father support in life, with a change at age 19.

meaning: Mercury in the 4th house with Sun in the 3rd, 5th or 11th and Jupiter in the 9th forms a raja-yoga in Lal Kitab, though Mercury in the 4th is heavy on the mother.
inference: Rise in status and fortune, at some cost to the mother's wellbeing.

meaning: When Rahu and Ketu are in a bad Lal Kitab state and Mars sits in the 7th, the wife and mother are said to suffer and a bad Mercury harms business.
inference: Trouble for wife and mother, plus business setbacks tied to Mercury.

meaning: Saturn in the 2nd house under the influence of the 6th, 8th or 12th is said to give a poor father, unwise children and trouble with in-laws at marriage, but a good Moon in the 2nd, or Saturn in the 11th, improves results.
inference: Family and in-law troubles that ease if the Moon is good or Saturn is in the 11th, which brings honour.

meaning: Saturn in the 9th house gives good fruit if the native is charitable and Mercury is not in the 3rd, and Venus coming to the 2nd in the annual chart multiplies this ninefold.
inference: Large family and good Saturn results, with children arriving late but surviving.
variants: Venus in 2nd house of annual chart

meaning: The book says that at ages 22 or 34 a sister or daughter may be widowed when a planet sits in the 12th or a companion planet sits in the 3rd, excluding Mars.
inference: A widowhood risk for a female relative around two named ages.

meaning: Rahu in the 11th moving to the 1st house in the annual chart is said to make the 16th year very painful for the grandfather.
inference: A hard year for the paternal grandfather at age 16.

meaning: Rahu in the 11th house is said to bring wealth and property while the father is alive, but the father's own life is under strain.
inference: High wealth up to the father's Jupiter-age span of 16 years, with a difficult path for the father.

meaning: If Ketu sits with malefics, Jupiter or Sun is hurt by enemy planets and Venus and Moon are together, Ketu counts as debilitated and a son or grandson gets a wasting illness.
inference: Health trouble for a descendant when Ketu turns weak.

meaning: Ketu in the 8th house with Mercury and Venus placed in bad houses is said to make the wife's health poor.
inference: Chronic ill health for the spouse.

meaning: A Moon line on the palm running toward Mercury, Sun or another mount shows profit from sea voyages, trade or government travel respectively.
inference: Gains from travel and trade, chosen by which mount the Moon line points to.

meaning: For the annual chart, a trip shorter than 100 days is not counted as travel, and travel is split by sea to Moon, air to Jupiter and land to Venus, with Ketu ordering all movement.
inference: Sets the yardstick and planet owners used when reading travel in annual charts.

meaning: Annual Ketu in house 1 means a journey is planned but not made, or the person is back within 100 days; it is only paper travel if house 7 is empty.
inference: Travel plans stall or stay short that year.

meaning: Annual Ketu in house 2 means travel goes with a promotion, so both happen or neither does.
inference: Travel tied to career promotion.

meaning: Annual Ketu in house 4 means no travel that year, or only a trip to the mother's place.
inference: Little or no travel; home-bound year.

meaning: Annual Ketu in house 7 means a change of city is certain, and it is auspicious if house 1 is unaffected.
inference: Relocation that year, favourable when the 1st house is clean.

meaning: Annual Ketu in house 8 brings unwanted harmful travel unless Moon or Mars is in house 11, with a remedy of feeding dogs milk with sulphur for 15 days.
inference: Unwelcome travel that year, relieved by Moon or Mars in the 11th.

meaning: Annual Ketu in house 9 gives auspicious, favourable travel provided house 3 is not polluted.
inference: Good journeys, spoilt if the 3rd house is afflicted.

meaning: Annual Ketu in house 10 makes travel doubtful: doubly good if Saturn is benefic, otherwise doubly bad.
inference: Travel outcome swings with Saturn's condition.

meaning: Annual Ketu in house 12 gives promotion without transfer, and travel is gainful if houses 6 and 2 are good.
inference: Career progress at the same place; paying trips if the 2nd and 6th are sound.

meaning: Jupiter in the 10th house with Sun or Moon in the 2nd points to travel on official or royal matters.
inference: Government or official trips connected to career.

meaning: Moon in the 4th house supported by Jupiter in the 2nd or 9th, Sun in the 5th, or Venus and Mars in the 10th brings wealth through voyages and import-export.
inference: Money from overseas trade and sea travel.

meaning: On the palm, a Sun line on the Moon mount marks a necessary journey, and a mark on the Venus mount marks a return from a journey.
inference: Palm signs of compulsory travel and of coming back.

meaning: Lines on the Moon mount describe travel: ordinary trips, constant land travel with a Venus line, and overseas or government-necessary travel when a line heads toward the Sun or Mercury.
inference: Travel kind and profit read from the direction of lines on the Moon mount.
variants: Line toward Mercury: profitable business trips

meaning: A fate line that starts from a square mark at its base is also good, though not as good as one starting with a fish mark.
inference: Fate line is favourable but of lesser grade.

meaning: Sun with Mercury or Mercury with Jupiter placed facing the Moon is said to spoil the result of sea travel.
inference: Sea voyages go badly.

meaning: A planet very good or very bad in the birth chart also shows its effect during half the span of another planet's period, e.g. a very bad Mercury hurts at age 17.
inference: A strong or weak natal planet leaks its results into half the time of other planets' periods.

meaning: Lal Kitab aspects: Sun, Moon, Mercury and Venus see only the 7th; Mars sees the 4th, 7th, 8th; Jupiter the 5th, 7th, 9th; Saturn the 3rd, 7th, 10th.
inference: Fixed aspect table used by later Lal Kitab rules.

meaning: Lal Kitab treats Sun, Mars, Saturn, Rahu and Ketu as malefics, and Moon, Mercury, Venus and Jupiter as benefics.
inference: Fixed benefic and malefic list for later rules.

meaning: Planets that exchange houses or sit in each other's signs are called sathi, partner planets, and do not act as enemies since each is the other's tenant.
inference: Sign-exchanging planets act friendly to each other.

meaning: In Lal Kitab a planet is debilitated in the sign seventh from its exaltation sign, such as the Moon exalted in Taurus and debilitated in Scorpio.
inference: Defines debilitation from exaltation.

meaning: Lists the Lal Kitab meaning of each house from the 1st (self, health) to the 12th (expenses, foreign travel, losses).
inference: Reference table of house topics.

meaning: Rahu and Ketu act as the lord of the sign they occupy, so a debilitated lord makes them debilitated and an exalted lord makes them exalted.
inference: Rahu and Ketu take on the strength of their sign lord.
variants: Rahu in Sagittarius with Jupiter debilitated in Capricorn

meaning: Rahu in Aquarius with Saturn debilitated, Rahu aspecting the 5th, counts as debilitated and spoils the intellect, with a mischievous or criminal streak.
inference: Clouded judgement and wrong-doing tendency.

meaning: Rahu in Taurus with Saturn in a friendly sign counts as exalted, giving a calm but clever and shrewd trader.
inference: Quiet nature with sharp business sense.

meaning: Ketu in the 2nd and Rahu in the 8th with excessive temple worship is said to cause losses of Rahu things: in-law ties, stubborn fever, sudden accidents and unseen losses.
inference: Sudden losses and health or accident trouble linked to Rahu matters.

meaning: The deity to worship is chosen from the planet in the 9th or 5th house: Sun Vishnu, Moon Shiva, Mars Hanuman, Mercury Durga, Jupiter Brahma, Rahu Saraswati, Ketu Ganesh; worshipping many deities together brings sorrow.
inference: Advice to follow a single deity matched to the planet.
variants: Lord of sign if both empty

meaning: Moon in the 4th house and the native selling milk makes him poor.
inference: Poverty from a milk trade when the Moon is in the 4th.

meaning: Jupiter is good in Cancer, Scorpio and Pisces and bad in Taurus, Virgo and Capricorn, with mixed results in other signs.
inference: Sign-based strength table for Jupiter.

meaning: A good Jupiter in the 1st house gives excellent education, children and ancestral property, with extra gains by sign: Cancer fortune, Scorpio wealth and a son first, Pisces government gains.
inference: Strong learning, family and property results.

meaning: A good Jupiter in the 2nd house gives stored wealth, handsome looks, defeat of enemies and a large family, adjusted by sign.
inference: Wealth, family and victory over enemies.
variants: Cancer: good wife and business profit

meaning: A good Jupiter in the 3rd house gives lion-like courage, helpful neighbours and happiness from younger siblings, with sign variations.
inference: Courage, good neighbours and sibling support.

meaning: A bad Jupiter in the 3rd house makes the native cowardly, covetous and prone to throat and arm trouble, with a remedy of worshipping a girl child and floating offerings in water.
inference: Weak courage, fluctuating faith and income, and marriage shortfalls.
variants: Capricorn: wealth loss and education trouble

meaning: A bad Jupiter in the 4th house gives anger, restlessness, weak mother's happiness and fruitless travel, with sign effects.
inference: Domestic unrest and unproductive journeys.

meaning: A good Jupiter in the 5th house gives good education, wealth and skill in mathematics, economics and computing, with maternal uncle and aunt happy.
inference: Learning and money strength with relatives' support.

meaning: A bad Jupiter in the 5th gives incomplete child and education happiness, breathing disease and weak marriage, with remedies of refusing gifts, keeping a choti and giving bananas and laddus.
inference: Problems with children, studies and breathing health.
variants: Capricorn: weak mother and property happiness

meaning: A good Jupiter in the 6th house brings divine help, last-minute success and protection from enemies and disease, with sign blends.
inference: Protection and late wins against enemies and illness.

meaning: A bad Jupiter in the 6th makes new enemies keep appearing and hurts an uncle's married life, with remedies of watering peepal and feeding girls halwa.
inference: Persistent enemies and relative's marriage trouble.

meaning: A bad Jupiter in the 8th harms the maternal uncle's marriage and brings high expenses and weak house and vehicle happiness, with turmeric and laddu remedies.
inference: Expense pressure and domestic asset shortfalls.

meaning: A good Jupiter in the 9th gives knowledge of religious language, full child happiness and the ability to turn a person into a yogi, with sign effects.
inference: Religious bent, children and fortune.

meaning: A bad Jupiter in the 9th makes the native an atheist with fewer children and foot trouble, with remedies like truthfulness, Ganga bath and a ghee lamp.
inference: Loss of faith, children and elder-sibling troubles.
variants: Capricorn: elder siblings and income low

meaning: A bad Jupiter in the 10th gives sign-specific harm: health trouble in Virgo, stomach injury and weak luck in Capricorn, with stick, horse-feeding and coin remedies.
inference: Career-house Jupiter trouble in health and luck.
variants: Capricorn: stomach injury and weak luck

meaning: A good Jupiter in the 11th house gives happiness from younger siblings, a good marriage, house, vehicle and servants.
inference: Gains, family comfort and domestic help.

meaning: A bad Jupiter in the 11th may leave the native without a house or proper funeral, make the father's wealth useless and ruin marriage, with remedies involving the father's belongings and charity at a cremation ground.
inference: Loss of inheritance, unstable worship and marriage.

meaning: A good Jupiter in the 12th house makes the native a giver who never begs, and those who hurt him ruin themselves.
inference: Self-respect, generosity and protection from enemies.

meaning: The Sun is good in Aries, Leo and Sagittarius and bad in Gemini, Libra and Aquarius.
inference: Sign-based strength table for the Sun.

meaning: A good Sun in the 1st house gives a benevolent, independent person of high government rank, with good father, education and children.
inference: Authority, education and family comfort.

meaning: A bad Sun in the 1st gives anger, harsh speech, government trouble, blood pressure and eye disease, with wheat and jaggery donation as remedy.
inference: Temper, official trouble and eye or pressure ailments.

meaning: A good Sun in the 2nd house makes a trader and donor with subdued enemies and government gain.
inference: Business success, honour and enemies kept down.

meaning: A good Sun in the 4th house gives land, property and vehicle happiness, a wife in government service and gain from transport or foreign travel.
inference: Property comfort and travel-linked income.

meaning: A good Sun in the 5th house gives full education and children, progress after children are born and good fortune and health.
inference: Children, learning and general luck.

meaning: A good Sun in the 6th house gives gain from government, quick temper and firm resolve, and he serves sisters.
inference: Official gains and strong will.

meaning: A good Sun in the 12th house makes a free-spirited, pure-hearted and religious person with an open courtyard in the house.
inference: Spiritual, clean-minded life.

meaning: The Moon is good in Taurus, Virgo and Capricorn and bad in Cancer, Scorpio and Pisces.
inference: Sign-based strength table for the Moon.

meaning: A good Moon in the 1st house gives a wise, benevolent person who gains from sea travel, is obedient to his mother and lives long.
inference: Good life span, mother's bond and sea-travel gains.

meaning: A good Moon in the 2nd house gives a cheerful, respected person who receives ancestral property.
inference: Respect and inheritance.

meaning: Mars is good in Taurus, Virgo and Capricorn and bad in Cancer, Scorpio and Pisces.
inference: Sign-based strength table for Mars.

meaning: A bad Mars in the 9th spoils one's luck, causes losses in fights and makes an atheist, with remedies of serving the brother's wife and donating masoor dal.
inference: Weak luck and faith with conflict losses.

meaning: A bad Mars in the 12th makes works get spoiled and gives an ungrateful nature, with remedies like no rusty weapons and Hanuman offerings.
inference: Failed efforts and weak marriage in some signs.
variants: Leo: marriage poor, younger siblings low

meaning: Mercury is good in Gemini, Libra and Aquarius and bad in Aries, Leo and Sagittarius.
inference: Sign-based strength table for Mercury.

meaning: A bad Mercury in the 3rd gives lisping speech and a wandering nature, with alum, moong and bird-feeding remedies.
inference: Speech faults and restless life, with sign-specific losses.
variants: Leo: property and mother low, accident risk

meaning: A bad Mercury in the 4th lowers the mother's happiness, makes the native timid and brings contact with a widow, with milk-washed dhak leaves and jaggery remedies.
inference: Home and mother troubles, timidity.

meaning: A bad Mercury in the 7th mainly harms marriage in Sagittarius and reduces children and education in other signs, with remedies of serving girls and a black cow.
inference: Marriage and children troubles.
variants: Sagittarius: mother low, own marriage poor

meaning: A bad Mercury in the 9th makes the native a slave of others, lisping and unreliable, with remedies like avoiding green and burying silver.
inference: Dependence and mistrust, sign-wise losses.

meaning: Venus is good in Cancer, Scorpio and Pisces and bad in Taurus, Virgo and Capricorn.
inference: Sign-based strength table for Venus.

meaning: Saturn is good in Gemini, Libra and Aquarius, bad in Aries, Leo and Sagittarius, and also gives good results in Taurus, Virgo and Capricorn.
inference: Sign-based strength table for Saturn.

meaning: Rahu is a shadow planet, neither good nor bad itself, and acts according to the planet whose sign it occupies.
inference: Rahu's result depends on its sign lord.

meaning: A good Rahu in the 1st house gives a king-like nature, a good in-law family and spending on pious works.
inference: Wealth and respect from the maternal side.

meaning: A bad Rahu in the 1st makes the native meddlesome, with head injury risk, no helper in bad times and job changes, with water-floating remedies.
inference: Interference, instability and head injury risk.

meaning: A bad Rahu in the 3rd lowers younger siblings' fortune, brings bad neighbours, arm injury and wasted money on friends, with coriander floating and no ivory at home.
inference: Sibling and neighbour trouble, cheating and arm injury.

meaning: A bad Ketu in the 9th makes an atheist who neglects parents and guru, with thigh and spine trouble, with gold-keeping and dog-serving remedies.
inference: Loss of faith and duty, and back or thigh ailments.

meaning: When two planets are together or aspect each other their nature changes: a bad planet gives good in the first half of life and bad in the second, and a good planet the opposite.
inference: Results flip between life halves for combined planets.

meaning: Moon and Mercury together give house-wise results: 2nd father's happiness and wealth, 4th low mother and property, 5th more daughters, 7th rich but unhappy, 10th weak wife happiness.
inference: Mixed results by the house of the Moon-Mercury pair.

meaning: Moon and Venus together are like muddy water, hurting mother and wife, with house-wise outcomes from healer in the 2nd to government gain in the 10th.
inference: Mixed fortune that damages mother and wife matters by house.

meaning: Mars and Saturn together in houses 2 or 3 make the native lose specific houses' things depending on the sign they occupy, with the Mars-sign houses always suffering.
inference: Loss in listed house areas for each sign of the pair.

meaning: Method rules: never judge on one planet, run any remedy for 43 days, weeks or months, start the next two weeks later, and read 'happiness low' as separation, quarrel, distance or early loss.
inference: Gives reading and remedy discipline, no testable chart condition.

meaning: Saturn in Sagittarius, normally weak, becomes good when Jupiter is in a good sign: Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces or Sagittarius.
inference: Saturn's bad result is cancelled by a well-placed Jupiter.

meaning: A set of quick Lal Kitab remedies: oil, coconut and grain offerings for Saturn and Rahu trouble, accidents, delayed marriage, business and house problems and poor marks.
inference: Offerings and feeding acts to calm the named troubles.

meaning: Moon placed outside the 2nd and 4th houses, especially in the 3rd, 6th, 8th, 10th, 11th or 12th, or Ketu in the 4th, marks a mother's debt (matru rin).
inference: Karmic debt towards the mother shows up as trouble in mother matters.

meaning: Jupiter in the 9th with Mercury in Sagittarius or Pisces creates a father's debt through Mercury.
inference: Father-linked karmic debt.

meaning: Saturn in the 9th with Mercury in Capricorn or Aquarius creates a father's debt through Mercury.
inference: Father-linked karmic debt.

meaning: For father's debt with afflicted Sun, the family collects equal money and holds a yajna in a temple, over 40-43 weeks.
inference: Shared ritual spending to settle the Sun-linked debt.

meaning: For father's debt with afflicted Moon, the family collects equal silver and throws it in flowing water.
inference: Shared silver offering to settle the Moon-linked debt.

meaning: For father's debt with afflicted Mars, the family pools money and organises a free medical camp.
inference: Shared charity for health to settle the Mars-linked debt.

meaning: For father's debt with afflicted Mercury, the family burns yellow shells together and puts the ashes in flowing water.
inference: Shared water ritual to settle the Mercury-linked debt.

meaning: For father's debt with afflicted Jupiter, the family donates money together at a temple.
inference: Shared temple giving to settle the Jupiter-linked debt.

meaning: For a father-debt (pitru rin) linked to an afflicted Venus, the family jointly pays for fodder for 100 cows over a 40-43 week programme.
inference: The tradition says this shared act eases the ancestral debt and the Venus-related troubles tied to it.

meaning: A Jupiter-linked ancestral debt (pitra rin) is present when Jupiter's enemy planets sit in the houses that belong to Jupiter in the Lal Kitab scheme.
inference: The tradition says the native's efforts fail near the finish and help promised by elders arrives slowly.
variants: Jupiter's own Lal Kitab houses are 2, 5, 9, 11 and 12; enemy planets there trigger it

meaning: A Sun-linked self debt (swa rin) is present when Sun's enemy planets occupy the houses assigned to the Sun in Lal Kitab.
inference: The tradition says the native's own effort is blocked and recognition comes late in life.
variants: Sun's own Lal Kitab houses are 1, 5 and 9; Saturn, Rahu or Venus there is the typical trigger

meaning: A Moon-linked mother debt (matru rin) arises when planets hostile to the Moon sit in the Moon's Lal Kitab houses.
inference: The tradition says the home lacks peace and money leaks away without a clear reason.
variants: Moon's own Lal Kitab houses are 1, 2, 4 and 6; Rahu, Ketu or Saturn there trigger it

meaning: A Venus-linked wife debt (stri rin) is formed when Venus's enemy planets occupy houses that Lal Kitab gives to Venus.
inference: The tradition says marriage and household relations need extra care and patience.
variants: Venus's own Lal Kitab houses are 2, 7 and 12; Sun, Moon or Rahu there trigger it

meaning: A Mars-linked brother debt (bhai rin) is present when planets inimical to Mars stand in Mars's Lal Kitab houses.
inference: The tradition says family and property quarrels drag on for years.
variants: Mars's own Lal Kitab houses are 1, 3, 8 and 10; Mercury or Ketu there are the usual triggers

meaning: A Mercury-linked sister debt (behen rin) is present when Mercury's enemy planets sit in Mercury's Lal Kitab houses.
inference: The tradition says relations with sisters and daughters stay strained and speech or business deals bring trouble.
variants: Mercury's own Lal Kitab houses are 3, 6, 7, 8 and 12; Moon there is the classic trigger

meaning: A Saturn-linked oppressor debt (zalimana rin) is present when Saturn's enemies occupy Saturn's Lal Kitab houses.
inference: The tradition says hardship comes through land, the house itself and dealings with workers or servants.
variants: Saturn's own Lal Kitab houses are 7, 8, 10 and 11; Sun or Moon there trigger it

meaning: A Rahu-linked unborn debt (ajanma rin) is present when planets hostile to Rahu sit in Rahu's Lal Kitab houses.
inference: The tradition says sudden reversals arrive from a direction the native did not watch.
variants: Rahu's own Lal Kitab houses are 3, 6 and 12; Sun, Venus or Mars there trigger it

meaning: A Ketu-linked divine debt (daivi rin) is present when Ketu's enemy planets stand in Ketu's Lal Kitab houses.
inference: The tradition says peace of mind is disturbed and there is persistent worry about children.
variants: Ketu's own Lal Kitab houses are 6 and 12; Moon, Mars or Sun there trigger it

meaning: A planet is called sleeping when the house it aspects holds no planet, so it neither helps nor harms actively.
inference: The tradition says benefic sleeping planets delay their gifts while malefic ones hold back their harm until woken by remedy.
variants: Sleeping Jupiter, Venus or Moon delays good results
Sleeping Saturn, Rahu or Ketu suppresses bad results

meaning: A house that contains no planet and receives no aspect is treated as a sleeping house.
inference: The tradition says the matters of that house stay dormant and give little result until activated.

meaning: When both the first and seventh houses are empty, the whole chart is classed as a sleeping chart (soya teva).
inference: The tradition says life results are delayed and come late for the native.
variants: Same test applied with houses 1 and 7 counted from the Moon

meaning: A sleeping Jupiter is said to wake up when the native reaches age 16, Jupiter's maturity age.
inference: The tradition says Jupiter's benefits (learning, guidance, luck) begin to show from around that age.

meaning: A sleeping Sun is said to stir when the native turns 22, the Sun's maturity age.
inference: The tradition says authority, confidence and standing begin to improve around that age.

meaning: A sleeping Moon is said to awaken at age 24, the Moon's maturity age.
inference: The tradition says mental calm and support from mother and home improve from about that age.

meaning: A sleeping Venus is said to become active at age 25, Venus's maturity age.
inference: The tradition says marriage, comforts and partnership matters begin to open up around that age.

meaning: A sleeping Mars is said to rouse at age 28, Mars's maturity age.
inference: The tradition says courage, drive and property-related gains pick up from about that age.

meaning: A sleeping Mercury is said to wake at age 34 in this source, though other Lal Kitab texts say 32.
inference: The tradition says business skill, speech and trade results start to firm up around that age.
variants: Alternative wake-up age 32 in other Lal Kitab sources

meaning: A sleeping Saturn is said to come alive at age 36, Saturn's maturity age.
inference: The tradition says career steadiness and reward for past hard work start to appear around that age.

meaning: A sleeping Rahu is said to stir at age 42, Rahu's maturity age.
inference: The tradition says sudden worldly shifts and unusual openings can begin from about that age.

meaning: A sleeping Ketu is said to become active at age 48, Ketu's maturity age.
inference: The tradition says detachment, spiritual turn and changes around offspring matters appear from about that age.

meaning: If the third house is empty, Jupiter placed elsewhere is considered asleep and its outcome depends on where Saturn sits.
inference: The tradition says Jupiter's benefits are conditional on Saturn's house, and a water-filled clay pot before auspicious events is the stated aid.
variants: Jupiter's result read from Saturn in house 1, 4, 7 or 10 versus dusthana houses

meaning: With an empty third house, Saturn is treated as sleeping and its results show only when Saturn reaches the lagna in the yearly (varshphal) chart at ages 11, 23, 36, 48, 57, 72, 84, 94, 105 and 119.
inference: The tradition says Saturn's good or bad fruit is held back until those years.
variants: Each listed age as a separate trigger year in the annual chart

meaning: In Lal Kitab a planet in the third house casts its look on the planet in the eleventh house, and Rahu or Venus in the third is best for that eleventh-house planet.
inference: The tradition says the eleventh-house planet's gains are supported when Rahu or Venus occupies the third.
variants: Rahu in 3 supporting a planet in 11
Venus in 3 supporting a planet in 11

meaning: When both the first and third houses hold planets, the eleventh-house planet gives its full results; if both are empty its results follow Saturn's placement.
inference: The tradition says the eleventh-house planet yields complete gains only with support from houses 1 and 3.
variants: Houses 1 and 3 both empty: 11th results read from Saturn's house

meaning: Lal Kitab links houses 8, 2, 6 and 12 in a chain where the eighth looks at the second, the second at the sixth and the sixth at the twelfth.
inference: The tradition says these four houses must be read together, since trouble or help passes along the chain.
variants: Planet in 8 affecting the 2nd house, then 6th, then 12th

meaning: Jupiter and Saturn sitting together in one house, best when it is a favourable house, forms the dharmi teva chart type.
inference: The tradition says the native gets higher help in hardship and malefic effects are reduced.

meaning: A planet untouched by enemy planets or enemy signs, with a benefic not joined to an enemy, gives the kayam grah chart type.
inference: The tradition says such a planet acts as a steady source of good fortune.

meaning: Two planets that exchange places through exalted, debilitated or fixed houses (for example Sun in 10 with Saturn in 5) form the saathi grah chart type, with Mercury as an exception.
inference: The tradition says the usual conflict between the two planets is reduced and results turn positive.
variants: Other Lal Kitab exchange pairs by exaltation/debilitation houses

meaning: Normally friendly planets can become enemies through placement, such as Venus in 6 with Sun in 7 or Libra, giving the mukabale grah chart type.
inference: The tradition says friendly pairs turn sour, with Venus and Mercury relations strained in this example.
variants: Venus in 6 with Sun in Libra

meaning: A planet sharing its house with its conflicting planet (for example Saturn with Sun) is called sleeping, which differs from combustion.
inference: The tradition says its results are muted, a sleeping debilitated planet stops giving bad results, and waking it needs actions tied to a friendly planet.
variants: Sleeping Jupiter woken by respecting elders and donating yellow items

meaning: A blind (andha) planet has muted results and cannot cast its aspect on other houses, and blindness overrides the sleeping state.
inference: The tradition says such a planet is unreliable and practical immediate remedies come before ritual ones.

meaning: If houses 1, 4, 7 and 10 are empty or hold only Rahu, Saturn or Ketu, the chart is called nabalig (immature).
inference: The tradition says the native's fortune stays undeveloped until strengthened by remedy or age.

meaning: Mercury standing alone in house 1, 4, 7 or 10 also makes the chart nabalig.
inference: The tradition says the same immature-horoscope weakness applies, with results held back.

meaning: When two planets are conjunct, Lal Kitab treats the pair as a masnui (artificial) planet that can strengthen or soften an afflicted root planet.
inference: The tradition says the artificial planet's own character is added to chart reading and used in remedies.
variants: Pair choice decides which artificial planet forms, as listed in the following rules

meaning: Mercury and Venus together form an artificial Sun in this source.
inference: The tradition says this artificial Sun governs health matters.
variants: Mercury with Venus in any single house

meaning: Sun and Jupiter together form an artificial Moon.
inference: The tradition says this artificial Moon governs the blood-related health of the parents.
variants: Sun with Jupiter in any single house

meaning: Sun and Mercury together form an artificial Mars.
inference: The tradition says this artificial Mars governs the longevity of the child.
variants: Sun with Mercury in any single house

meaning: Jupiter and Rahu together form an artificial Mercury.
inference: The tradition says this artificial Mercury governs reputation and public respect.
variants: Jupiter with Rahu in any single house

meaning: Sun and Venus together form an artificial Jupiter.
inference: The tradition says this artificial Jupiter governs childbirth.
variants: Sun with Venus in any single house

meaning: Rahu and Ketu together form an artificial Venus in this source.
inference: The tradition says this artificial Venus governs worldly comforts.

meaning: Jupiter with Venus, or Mars with Mercury, forms an artificial Saturn.
inference: The tradition says this artificial Saturn governs health and illness.

meaning: Mars with an exalted Saturn, or Saturn with a debilitated Sun, forms an artificial Rahu.
inference: The tradition says this artificial Rahu governs quarrels and conflicts.

meaning: Venus with an exalted Saturn, or Saturn with a debilitated Moon, forms an artificial Ketu.
inference: The tradition says this artificial Ketu governs comforts and luxuries.

meaning: For a problematic artificial Venus made by Rahu and Ketu, bury blue vitriol at sunset on a Thursday in a deserted grassy spot and feed a white dog milk or a milk sweet.
inference: The tradition says these acts correct the artificial Venus and ease comfort and relationship troubles.

meaning: A planet that is exalted or well placed should not have its items donated or gifted away, while receiving gifts of its items is good.
inference: The tradition says giving away a strong planet's articles weakens it and accepting them adds to its strength.
variants: Reverse for a debilitated planet: donate its items, avoid accepting them

meaning: When the Sun is debilitated in house 7 or weak in house 8, donating Sun-related items at midday is advised.
inference: The tradition says this donation reduces the Sun's weak effects on status and health of the father line.

meaning: With an exalted Moon in house 2 or 4, one should not give away silver, milk or rice.
inference: The tradition says giving these away drains the Moon's strength and its gifts of peace and money.

meaning: For the first house, the site lists a menu of fixes such as an unscissored blue thread on the right toe, a temporary nose piercing, yellow donations, a peepal tree and buried ghee.
inference: The tradition says any of these remedies eases troubles of the first house, though no rule for choosing among them is given.

meaning: For the first house, the page forbids gold at the neck and silver on the feet, advises an iron cupboard rather than wood, and says to fix rust but leave car dents.
inference: The tradition says following these prohibitions avoids aggravating the first house's difficulties.

meaning: For the first house, thread colours are set as red-violet-brown on the left toe and blue-violet-brown on the right, with saffron kept visible in the car.
inference: The tradition says these colours and the saffron balance the planetary pressure on the first house.

meaning: For the second house, the page lists not tallying expenses, iron donations, a neem tree, buried red ochre with honey, Tuesday Hanuman offerings, and clearing broken footwear and junk.
inference: The tradition says these steps support money and family matters of the second house.

meaning: For the second house, avoid gold or silver on the feet and a black purse, wear iron at the neck and carry two steel balls in the purse.
inference: The tradition says these restrictions protect wealth and speech under the second house.

meaning: For the second house, use a blue thread on the right toe, a yellow-grey-black thread on the left and put sindoor on the navel.
inference: The tradition says these thread and body marks steady the second-house planets.

meaning: For the third house, remedies include feeding boiled wheat to a cow on Sundays, a south-west mirror, floating four raw coals, silver in the purse and giving copper at a brother's house.
inference: The tradition says these acts help courage, siblings and effort matters of the third house.

meaning: For the third house, keep hair open instead of in a bun, avoid silver on the feet, a wooden bed and a black or red purse, and wear black thread at the neck.
inference: The tradition says these prohibitions prevent worsening of third-house results.

meaning: For the third house, tie a red-violet-brown thread on the right toe and a black-white-blue-grey one on the left, and put saffron on the navel.
inference: The tradition says these colours and the saffron mark pacify third-house influences.

meaning: For the fourth house, the page advises asking nothing from God, making no plans, keeping matters secret, burying ash, using cremation-ground borewell water and keeping two holeless copper pieces in the purse.
inference: The tradition says this restrained conduct and these objects protect home, mother and peace linked to the fourth house.

meaning: For the fourth house, a woman should not hand yellow items to her husband or eat his yellow leftovers, nor give him green leftovers, and should avoid a black purse.
inference: The tradition says these habits avoid harming the husband's fortune and the household under the fourth house.

meaning: For the fourth house, wear a yellow-black-grey thread on the right toe and brown-violet-red on the left, and keep saffron in the purse and locker.
inference: The tradition says these colours and the saffron strengthen fourth-house matters.

meaning: For the fifth house, the site lists barley in well water, an iron rod in a well, gurudwara gifts of besan or laddu, a turmeric-flour donation at 1/5 body weight, buried iron nails and coins, and turmeric lumps in the car.
inference: The tradition says these offerings support children and learning matters of the fifth house.

meaning: For the fifth house, avoid giving yellow things to the husband, Saturn worship or Saturn donations, sweets as charity, a black purse and black thread at the neck.
inference: The tradition says these abstentions prevent aggravation of fifth-house troubles.

meaning: For the fifth house, tie a black-white-blue-grey thread on the right toe and an orange-yellow-grey one on the left, with sindoor on the navel.
inference: The tradition says these colours and the navel mark tune the fifth-house influences.

meaning: For the sixth house, the page lists offerings of sugar, tea and iron utensils at a gurudwara, floating mixed grains in a river, 4 kg of potato in a river, a steel neck item, silver in the cash box and jaggery with turmeric for a cow.
inference: The tradition says these actions ease the enemy, debt and health themes of the sixth house.

meaning: For the sixth house, do not directly hand green items, stationery, money, a belt or trousers to the husband, and avoid gold at the neck, silver on the feet and a wooden cupboard.
inference: The tradition says avoiding these keeps sixth-house troubles from spreading into the marriage.

meaning: For the sixth house, use brown-violet-red thread on the right toe and blue-orange-yellow on the left, a three-knot blue waist thread for stomach trouble and turmeric on the navel.
inference: The tradition says these threads and the turmeric mark calm the sixth house and digestive complaints.

meaning: For the seventh house, the page lists Sunday wheat for a cow, cremation-ground borewell water, black urad in raw milk floated in a river, a south-east mirror, removing rusty iron and broken wood, fixing dripping taps and a silver-copper kada.
inference: The tradition says these steps support marriage and partnership matters of the seventh house.

meaning: For the seventh house, keep matters secret, make no plans, do not count money, and avoid silver on the feet, a black purse, black neck thread and gold at the neck.
inference: The tradition says this discipline avoids spoiling the seventh house's results.

meaning: For the seventh house, thread colours are orange-yellow-grey on the right toe and blue-grey-black on the left, with two copper pieces and saffron kept in the purse or locker.
inference: The tradition says these colours and items settle seventh-house influences.

meaning: For the eighth house, the site lists rice and mirror gifts at a gurudwara, jaggery in a river, a covered pot of jaggery, lentil and honey floated, feeding flour to fish, iron and oil donations at a charity school, and buried nails and coins.
inference: The tradition says these remedies soften the eighth house's hardships and sudden troubles.

meaning: For the eighth house, avoid Saturn worship or donations, giving sweets at a temple, a wooden bed, and gold or silver on the feet.
inference: The tradition says these prohibitions keep the eighth house from worsening.

meaning: For the eighth house, the thread on the right toe is blue-orange-yellow and on the left green-red-violet-brown.
inference: The tradition says these colour combinations balance eighth-house planets.

meaning: For the ninth house, remedies include burying copper coins with alum and tin, an iron rod in a well, gurudwara gifts, a turmeric-flour donation at 1/9 body weight, a neem tree, whisky to the boss and an iron cupboard.
inference: The tradition says these actions strengthen luck, father and dharma themes of the ninth house.

meaning: For the ninth house, always keep hair tied in a bun, and avoid Saturn worship or donation, gold at the neck, silver on the feet and black neck thread.
inference: The tradition says these rules protect the ninth house from Saturn-type harm.

meaning: For the ninth house, use a blue-grey-black thread on the right toe and blue-white-grey on the left, sindoor on the navel and visible saffron in the car.
inference: The tradition says these colours and marks steady ninth-house fortune.

meaning: For the tenth house, the page advises asking nothing of God, no advance planning, secrecy, no red meat, cow urine at home, a red toe thread, iron rod and barley in a well, buried saffron and gold, and turmeric or milk on the navel.
inference: The tradition says this conduct and these objects support career and status matters of the tenth house.

meaning: For the tenth house, the only prohibitions are a black purse and a black thread at the neck.
inference: The tradition says avoiding these two items prevents harm to career results.

meaning: For the tenth house, tie a green-red-violet-brown thread on the right toe and blue-violet-brown-red-grey on the left.
inference: The tradition says these colours steady tenth-house planetary effects.

meaning: For the eleventh house, the site lists gurudwara gifts of rice, sugar and mirror, sugar equal to body weight or millet floated in a river, a husked coconut in a river, buried gold or a sugar-filled flute, saffron on the navel and iron to a passer-by.
inference: The tradition says these remedies support gains and friendships of the eleventh house.

meaning: For the eleventh house, never give sweets as donation or gift and avoid silver on the feet.
inference: The tradition says these two abstentions protect eleventh-house income.

meaning: For the eleventh house, the right toe thread is blue-white-grey and the left toe thread is blue-violet-brown.
inference: The tradition says these colours tune eleventh-house effects.

meaning: For the twelfth house, the page lists gold-soldered brass pieces and turmeric thrown in well water, gurudwara gifts, a jaggery-lentil-honey pot in a river, buried sesame, millet, tin and nails, iron at a cremation ground and bronze in the car.
inference: The tradition says these actions ease losses and expenses linked to the twelfth house.

meaning: For the twelfth house, do not worship Saturn or donate its items, avoid gold or silver on the feet and a black purse, while a black neck thread is recommended.
inference: The tradition says these rules keep twelfth-house results from deteriorating.

meaning: For the twelfth house, the right toe takes a blue-violet-brown-red-grey thread, the left a plain blue one, and sindoor goes on the navel.
inference: The tradition says these colours and the mark settle twelfth-house influences.

meaning: The page claims that running after a task actively makes it fail.
inference: The tradition says patient non-chasing, with surrender to God, is the right approach to getting work done.

meaning: The page claims that telling others about a pending task makes it fail.
inference: The tradition says keeping unfinished work private protects its success.

meaning: The page claims that praying to God for one specific outcome makes that outcome fail.
inference: The tradition says one should leave the result to God rather than demand a particular one.

meaning: The page claims that too much talk about a task spoils it.
inference: The tradition says restraint in speech keeps work on track.

meaning: The page claims that working out gains or outcomes before a task is complete spoils it.
inference: The tradition says advance calculation invites failure, so one should finish first.

meaning: The page claims that celebrating or feeling joy about a plan before it is done makes the plan fail.
inference: The tradition says early happiness invites reversal, so celebration should wait for completion.

meaning: The page claims that boasting or speaking from ego brings bad news.
inference: The tradition says humility in speech protects against setbacks.

meaning: The page discourages keeping a written account of one's expenses.
inference: The tradition says writing out spending is thought to hurt money flow, though this is a stated belief and not a tested rule.

meaning: The page discourages counting money again and again and warns that talking about how income will be spent before it arrives reduces it.
inference: The tradition says repeated counting and pre-spending talk reduces incoming money.

meaning: The page says not to fix a set portion of income as a pledge to God, while spontaneous charity is acceptable.
inference: The tradition says a fixed tithe is not favoured in this school, and giving should be unplanned.

meaning: The page advises against planning a celebration party for an event ahead of time, as it makes the event fail.
inference: The tradition says early party planning invites the event to collapse, so festivities should follow success.

meaning: As a home and office hygiene tip, windows should be fitted with glass.
inference: The tradition says glass windows keep the premises in good order and support household luck.

meaning: The home should hold only a single Ganesh idol.
inference: The tradition says one idol is proper and several idols disturb the household's balance.

meaning: Faulty electrical items, stopped clocks and broken clay objects should be cleared from the home.
inference: The tradition says keeping broken or stalled items invites stagnation and obstruction in the household.

meaning: A mirror should be placed on the east side of the home.
inference: The tradition says an east-facing mirror brings in positive energy and benefits the household.

meaning: Keep stationery used at home or office from being red.
inference: Tradition says red stationery brings friction or loss in work and money matters.

meaning: Three offerings: rice starch poured at a cremation ground, plain rice kheer floated in a river, and curd given at a temple.
inference: Tradition says these gifts to Saturn-Rahu-linked places and to water and temple ease long-standing troubles.

meaning: Do not place a temple or puja space in the south-west corner of the house.
inference: Tradition says a puja place in the south-west corner brings domestic unrest and blocks luck.

meaning: Do not keep a mirror where it reflects the bed.
inference: Tradition says a mirror facing the bed disturbs sleep and strains the marriage.

meaning: Keep only one Ganesh idol in the house, not several.
inference: Tradition says several Ganesh idols at home weaken Ketu-Mercury results and bring confusion.

meaning: Do not offer silver foil or leaf to Hanuman.
inference: Tradition says silver offered to Hanuman works against the native, since silver belongs to Moon and Venus and Hanuman to Mars.

meaning: Burn four dry red chillies with their stalks in the house.
inference: Tradition says this burning drives out the evil eye and household obstruction.

meaning: Wave a fistful of salt anticlockwise round the person to remove the evil eye.
inference: Tradition says the salt absorbs the evil eye and is then thrown or flushed away.

meaning: Float 400 grams of whole turmeric lumps in flowing river water.
inference: Tradition says this Jupiter-linked offering clears delays in luck, marriage or children.

meaning: Hand out boondi prasad at a temple for 15 days without eating it or taking it home.
inference: Tradition says giving away the prasad fully sends the trouble away with it.

meaning: On Tuesdays offer only sindoor to Hanuman, or else give away all the prasad and eat none of it.
inference: Tradition says this Mars remedy works only when nothing offered comes back to the giver.

meaning: Feed cows plain bread daily, or a seven-grain mix, or half-baked roti with turmeric.
inference: Tradition says feeding cows reduces the harm of troubled Jupiter, Venus and Moon.

meaning: Offer wheat flour mixed with turmeric, without water, at the roots of a peepal tree for four days.
inference: Tradition says this is a Jupiter-Sun offering that helps blocked good fortune.

meaning: For Saturn, do not donate coins, oil or other Saturn items, though worship of Saturn is fine.
inference: Tradition says donating Saturn items weakens Saturn's help while worship does not.

meaning: Do not immerse a Ganesh idol in water.
inference: Tradition says floating Ganesh brings poverty, so the idol should be kept or placed respectfully elsewhere.

meaning: Avoid wearing or using white things after sunset.
inference: Tradition says white after dark disturbs Moon and Venus matters like peace and domestic life.

meaning: Keep no Shiva idol or shivling in the home temple, though worship of Shiva is allowed.
inference: Tradition says a household shivling needs strict upkeep and can give Rahu-Ketu trouble if neglected.

meaning: Several puja cautions: no clockwise round on the south side, no prasad or water taken there, and no oil lamp or bell in puja (ghee lamp is fine).
inference: Tradition says these habits strain Mars and Saturn matters and bring obstruction.

meaning: Do not give sweets to anyone directly with your own hand.
inference: Tradition says handing sweets over directly passes your luck to the receiver.

meaning: Keep ghee in a glass vial inside the cash box and locker.
inference: Tradition says this holds wealth and brings steady money flow.

meaning: Donate black urad on Saturdays for head injury, tiredness and leg pain.
inference: Tradition says Saturn is appeased by black urad and this eases such Saturn-linked complaints.

meaning: Keep water drawn from a cremation ground (handpump or well) hidden in the north of the home.
inference: Tradition says this Saturn-Rahu remedy protects the house from hidden troubles.

meaning: Get the nose pierced and keep it for 100 hours, and tie a black or yellow thread on the toe.
inference: Tradition says this Venus-Rahu remedy corrects luck and removes obstruction.

meaning: Do not count money in public or plan, discuss or disclose money matters.
inference: Tradition says talking about money plans leaks the gains from them.

meaning: In Lal Kitab the ascendant is always house 1 with Aries as its fixed sign, and later houses follow 2 to 12 with fixed signs, so house numbers replace sign and lordship ideas.
inference: This is the base convention and gives no outcome by itself.
variants: Same fixed-house convention applied to the Moon chart
Same fixed-house convention applied to the annual chart

meaning: Lal Kitab drops lagna lord and dhana lord ideas, treats planets sharing a house together even in the annual chart, and ties each planet's effect to its own things and relatives.
inference: It is a method statement and gives no direct result.

meaning: In Lal Kitab, Rahu and Ketu need not be seven houses apart and in the annual chart can fall together, and each planet acts independently.
inference: Tradition notes this departs from the classical 180-degree node axis.

meaning: Each of the nine planets is a fixed knot with its own sign, exaltation, debilitation, pakka house, friends and enemies, and effects at set ages.
inference: This introduces the planet table the rest of the system uses and gives no outcome.

meaning: Planets are grouped: Jupiter, Sun and good Mars together, Saturn-Rahu-Ketu as the sinful group, Venus and Moon as female significators, and Mercury as the mixer.
inference: The grouping guides which planets are expected to help or harm each other.

meaning: Jupiter's friends are Sun, Moon and Mars, its enemies are Venus and Mercury, and Saturn, Rahu and Ketu are neutral to it.
inference: Friendship decides whether planets with Jupiter help or harm it.
variants: Jupiter conjunct Venus read as enemy placement
Jupiter conjunct Sun read as friendly placement

meaning: Sun's friends are Jupiter, Mars and Moon, its enemies are Venus, Saturn, Rahu and Ketu, and Mercury is neutral.
inference: Friendship decides how other planets treat Sun when they share or look at its house.
variants: Sun conjunct Saturn read as enemy placement

meaning: Saturn's friends are Venus and Rahu, its enemies are Sun, Moon and Mars, and Jupiter and Ketu are neutral.
inference: Friendship decides how other planets treat Saturn in a shared house.
variants: Saturn conjunct Moon read as enemy placement

meaning: Rahu's friends are Mercury, Saturn and Ketu and its enemies Sun and Venus, while Ketu's friends are Venus and Rahu and its enemies Moon and Mars; Rahu is called the head and Ketu the feet.
inference: Node friendships decide whether a planet with Rahu or Ketu is helped or harmed.

meaning: Some enmities run one way only: Moon dislikes Venus though Venus likes Moon, and Jupiter is hostile to Venus, Mars to Saturn, Moon to Mercury.
inference: The direction of dislike decides which planet suffers in a shared house.

meaning: If Mercury or Moon sits in house 2 or 4 they help Jupiter fully, and Rahu in house 2 with Jupiter becomes subordinate to Jupiter.
inference: Tradition says Jupiter's results stay protected in this setup and its usual enemies do not harm it.

meaning: Each planet gives results across a set number of years: Jupiter 16, Sun 22, Moon 24, Venus 25, Mars 28, Mercury 34, Saturn 36, Rahu 42, Ketu 48 and Rahu-Ketu together 45.
inference: A planet's matters ripen in its own age band, with half or quarter effects possible mid-way.
variants: Rahu and Ketu together as 45 years

meaning: A planet that is not in its own full-strength state uses a reduced set of ages depending on its company, with default ages of Jupiter 16, Sun 22 and Moon 24.
inference: Weak or accompanied planets deliver results at borrowed ages instead of their own.

meaning: In the annual chart a year is cut into three four-month blocks, each ruled by a different planet according to the year's house position.
inference: Different parts of the year carry the influence of different planets.

meaning: A malefic's bad results do not start before its fixed time nor good help last beyond it, except for about 40 extra days at the edges, and signs can show up to 40 days before a new year or period.
inference: Early signs about 40 days ahead hint at how the coming period will go.

meaning: About 40 days before the year turns, items of friendly planets appearing predict a good coming year, while signs of papi planets like theft, false cases or travel loss predict continued bad effects.
inference: Observed events before the year change show whether the next year is good or bad.

meaning: In a clash the relative strengths are Sun 9, Moon 8, Venus 7, Jupiter 6, Mars 5, Mercury 4, Saturn 3, Rahu 2 and Ketu 1 out of 9.
inference: The planet with the higher number wins in a clash and can be used to remedy a lower one.

meaning: A planet outside its own, exalted, debilitated or pakka house gives doubtful rashi phal that can be remedied, while one in such a house gives graha phal that is fixed.
inference: Tradition says fixed-state planets give unchangeable results while others can be improved by remedy.

meaning: Graha phal is compared to a king and rashi phal to a minister, so in bad times a rashi-phal planet can be used as a helper for the remedy.
inference: Remedies should work through the changeable helper planet, not the fixed one.

meaning: All nine planets complete one round in 35 years in the order Jupiter, Sun, Moon, Venus, Mars, Mercury, Saturn, Rahu, Ketu, and in the second round planets that gave bad results earlier do not repeat them.
inference: Life is read in 35-year cycles, and the second cycle is milder for planets that were bad in the first.

meaning: The 35-year cycle may start from a planet other than Jupiter and from a later year, and sub-periods inside it follow a lookup table.
inference: The starting planet shifts which planet's results come at which age.

meaning: The planet of the weekday of birth is the janam-din planet, with Sun Sunday through Saturn Saturday, and Rahu governs evening and Ketu pre-dawn.
inference: The birth-day planet marks a remediable influence on the chart.

meaning: The planet of the birth time of day is Jupiter after sunrise, Sun before noon, Moon on moonlit night, Venus on new-moon night, Mars at noon, Mercury afternoon to evening, Saturn on black night, Rahu at full evening and Ketu at dawn.
inference: The birth-time planet marks a fixed influence.

meaning: The planet of the birth day is the remediable rashi phal and the planet of the birth time is the fixed graha phal, with a worked example of a Monday evening birth where Moon and Rahu apply.
inference: Tradition says trouble from the birth-time planet is handled through the birth-day planet.
variants: Monday evening: Moon as day planet, Rahu as time planet

meaning: If Mercury is with bad planets or in houses holding Sun or Saturn, Sun and Saturn weaken, Mars turns bad and Rahu weakens, so Mars gives no good result anywhere.
inference: Tradition says this Mercury affliction spoils a whole group of planets and Mars especially.

meaning: If house 10 is afflicted by mutually hostile or poor planets the chart becomes andha (blind) and all planets act like Saturn in blind condition even in good houses.
inference: Tradition says such a chart gives poor results despite apparent good placements.
variants: House 1 afflicted version if the house number was misread

meaning: If Saturn sits in the 4th or 7th with planets seeing by day but not by night, the chart is nahorata (half-blind) and its planets work only by day.
